levels.title: The 4 risk levels
levels.1: Conditions are comparable to Canada. Take the precautions you would at home.
levels.2: There are some risks, or conditions could change. Take extra care and stay informed.
levels.3: Significant risks. Only go if it’s necessary. May affect your travel insurance.
levels.4: Serious risks to your safety. Don’t go. If you’re there, leave if it’s safe to do so.
duty.title: Duty-free allowance
duty.subtitle: Coming home to Canada · personal exemption
duty.handoffNote: Opens CBSA’s estimator for anything over your exemption.
duty.bis: Questions? Call the Border Information Service.
tier.under24.rule: Same-day trips don’t get a personal exemption.
tier.h24.rule: Away at least 24 hours: up to {amount}. Alcohol and tobacco aren’t included, and everything must be with you.
tier.h48.rule: Away at least 48 hours: up to {amount}, including alcohol and tobacco within the limits below.
tier.d7.rule: Away at least 7 days (don’t count the day you left; count the day you return): up to {amount}.
duty.spent: Value of goods bought or received abroad
duty.tobacco: I’m bringing tobacco or vaping products
duty.atNotIncluded.title: Alcohol and tobacco aren’t covered.
duty.atNotIncluded.under24: Same-day trips have no exemption, so duty and taxes apply to them.
duty.atNotIncluded.h24: The 24-hour exemption leaves them out, so you’ll pay duty and taxes on them. From 48 hours, they’re included within limits.
limits.title: Alcohol and tobacco limits
limits.age: You must be of legal drinking age where you enter Canada: 18 in Alberta, Manitoba and Quebec, 19 elsewhere.
limits.vaping.about: in up to 12 devices and containers
limits.stamped: Cigarettes, manufactured tobacco, tobacco sticks and vaping products must be stamped “duty paid Canada droit acquitté”. You must be 18 or older.
rules.title: Good to know
rules.withYou: Everything you claim must be with you when you cross the border.
rules.shipLater: After 7 days, goods other than alcohol and tobacco can follow by mail or courier. Declare them all when you arrive (Form BSF192).
rules.declareAll: Declare everything you bought or received abroad, including duty-free shop purchases and gifts.
rules.perPerson: Each person, children included, has their own exemption. You can’t pool or transfer them.
rules.noCombine: Exemptions don’t add up: a 9-day trip still gets one exemption, not two.
rules.cash: Carrying {amount} or more in cash or monetary instruments? Report it when you cross.
tip.arrivecan.title: Flying home?
tip.arrivecan.body: At 10 major Canadian airports, you can make your customs declaration in ArriveCAN up to {hours} hours before your flight.
tip.surtax.title: Goods from the U.S.:
tip.surtax.body: Canada applies counter tariffs (surtaxes) to certain goods originating in the United States (not everything you buy there). The current list took effect September 8, 2026.
verdict.freeSub: You still have {left} left of your {allowance} exemption.
verdict.sameDay: Stay away 24 hours or more to qualify for a personal exemption.
verdict.overSub: Only the part over {allowance} is taxed. You’re bringing back {spent}.
verdict.cliffSub: Between 24 and 48 hours, going over {amount} means you can’t claim the exemption at all: duty and taxes apply to all {spent}. Stay at {amount} or less, or away 48 hours.
verdict.noneSub: Same-day trips don’t qualify for a personal exemption, so duty and taxes apply to everything.

sos.title: Emergency help abroad
sos.subtitle: For Canadians outside Canada · 24/7
sos.handoffNote: On travel.gc.ca. If it’s urgent, call instead.
sos.dangerIn: In {country}, call local emergency services first.
sos.dangerSub: Then contact Canada’s Emergency Watch and Response Centre, below.
sos.missing.title: We couldn’t load local details for {place}.
sos.missing.body: The contacts below work from anywhere.
sos.ewrcBody: Canadian citizens can reach the Emergency Watch and Response Centre, run by Global Affairs Canada in Ottawa, at any time by phone, text or email. Family in Canada can call on your behalf.
sos.ch.tollFreeNote: May not connect from every phone. If it fails, call the number below.
sos.ch.familyNote: Toll-free, for someone calling about a Canadian abroad
sos.scope: For Canadian citizens. The centre doesn’t answer questions about immigration, permanent residence or visas.
sos.next.lost: Lost or stolen passport: contact the nearest Canadian office as soon as you can. If you urgently need to travel, you can apply for an emergency passport, though not every office offers it.
sos.next.arrest: Arrested or detained: ask the authorities to notify the nearest Canadian office right away. Consular officers can’t get you out of jail or pay bail, but they can contact your family and give you a list of local lawyers.
sos.next.medical: Sick or injured: for urgent care, the nearest hospital is often the best option. The Government of Canada doesn’t pay medical bills, so contact your insurer.
sos.nextLink: What to do if things go wrong
